Nora H.: Heads-up — saw a 2.3x tail latency bump on the decode path for single-token requests on NGC-3 around 03:12 UTC. Attaching flame + trace in the thread.
perf-bot: profile uploaded: s3://redwood-profiles/1719801234/decode-single-token-flame.svg (summary: CPU hotpath in kernel_selector + memcpy)
Alex M.: I pulled the flame. Quick take: kernel selector picks `flash_fused` initially but immediately falls back to `paged_flash` at the first step when batch_size==1. Theres a memcpy in kv_page_align that only happens on the paged path.
Jonatan: can you paste the kernel_choice log lines? wondering which condition triggered fallback.
Nora H.: paste from the agent logs:
```
[03:12:07.431] batch_size=1 seq_len_hint=1 model=redwood/open-7b kernel_choice=flash_fused
[03:12:07.431] kernel_init: layout_check_failed (tile_size mismatch) => schedule fallback to paged_flash
[03:12:07.432] paged_flash::kv_page_align: memcpy 48KB
[03:12:07.432] decode_step: latency=18.4ms
```
Alex M.: that `layout_check_failed` is the key. Our layout verifier rejects because continuous-batching sets a per-request seq_hint=1 and the optimized fused kernel expects a min_tile of 16 for efficient warps. When rejection happens we go to paged_flash which incurs the 48KB memcpy per request.
Sara P.: hypothesis: two orthogonal issues — (A) selector min_tile threshold too aggressive for single-token streams, (B) KV page alignment code not no-op for very small KV (introduces memcpy). Both cause wasted cycles.
Jonatan: agree. I ran a micro-bench on devbox (A100) with a synthetic single-token workload. Numbers:
```
kernel=flash_fused batch=1 seq=1 throughput=~55 tok/s latency=12ms
kernel=paged_flash batch=1 seq=1 throughput=~22 tok/s latency=40ms (memcpy ~35% of time)
```
Alex M.: Yea that matches the flame. Also noticed the continuous-batcher sometimes sets seq_hint to 0 for streaming requests which trips another code path that prefers safety.
Nora H.: immediate mitigation options: 1) relax min_tile -> allow flash_fused for seq_hint==1 on supported archs, 2) short-circuit kv_page_align when kv_size < 8KB to avoid memcpy, 3) emit telemetry `kernel_fallback_reason` for next 48h. Thoughts?
Sara P.: implement 3 first (fast). For 1/2 we should add a canary behind runtime flag. Changing tile thresholds can affect throughput on medium batches; need perf-guard.
Alex M.: I'll prototype a runtime flag `enable_smallbatch_fused=true` and a kv_align fastpath. Can run canaries across two pods in us-west-2.
Jonatan: add regression test: synthetic single-token stream + perf harness that asserts median latency < 20ms and fallback_count==0.
Nora H.: agree. Owners: Alex = patch + perf runs, Sara = unit/regression tests, Jonatan = validate telemetry + dashboards. I'll open PLT ticket and link patch.
perf-bot: created perf ticket PLT-321 and benchmark job 1719801800 (queued) :eyes:
Alex M.: rough plan timeline:
- today: telemetry + quick kv fastpath (opt-in flag)
- tomorrow: canary + perf runs
- EOW: roll to stable if no regressions
Nora H.: thanks. If we see any other single-token spikes, @channel call it out and tag `eng-runtime` so we can correlate.
Sara P.: one more note — verify that quantized kernels (int8) follow same selector path; otherwise we'll regress int8 latency.
Alex M.: will include int8 in canary matrix.
Nora H.: closing loop here, will post results once the canary finishes. :thumbsup:
